from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Place a sphere inside the cone.",
            "The sphere touches the cone's inner circle.",
            "The sphere also touches the slicing plane.",
            "The contact point is the conic focus.",
            "This creates the elegant Dandelin construction."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Dandelin Construction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=3, direction=DOWN).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*2+UP*0.5, RIGHT*2+UP*0.5, RIGHT*2+DOWN*0.5, LEFT*2+DOWN*0.5).rotate(PI/6, axis=RIGHT).set_fill(GRAY, opacity=0.5)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.5, color="#87CEEB").set_opacity(0.7)
        focus_dot = Dot(color="#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), FadeIn(plane))
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B3', 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#87CEEB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualizing tangency circle (conceptual)
        tangent_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#87CEEB").rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT).move_to(sphere.get_center())
        self.play(Create(tangent_circle))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#87CEEB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Move sphere to touch plane
        self.play(sphere.animate.move_to(plane.get_center() + UP*0.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Point P sits on our ellipse.",
            "Distances to two foci add up.",
            "Sum remains constant for every point.",
            "Tangent properties prove this sum invariant.",
            "Dandelin Spheres confirm the ellipse property."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Proving the Ellipse Property", lecture_lines)
        
        # Ellipse and Foci setup
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3, height=2, color=WHITE)
        f1 = Dot(color=BLUE)
        f2 = Dot(color=BLUE)
        f1.move_to(ellipse.get_center() + LEFT * 0.8)
        f2.move_to(ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.8)
        
        p = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        p.move_to(ellipse.point_from_proportion(0.2))
        
        path1 = Line(p.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color=BLUE_A)
        path2 = Line(p.get_center(), f2.get_center(), color=BLUE_B)
        
        # Position everything
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(ellipse, f1, f2, p, path1, path2), 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(ellipse), Create(p))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(f1), Create(f2), Create(path1), Create(path2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        # Update point P along ellipse
        path1.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(Line(p.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color=BLUE_A)))
        path2.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(Line(p.get_center(), f2.get_center(), color=BLUE_B)))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(p, ellipse), run_time=3)
        path1.remove_updater(path1.get_updaters()[0])
        path2.remove_updater(path2.get_updaters()[0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(PURPLE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(ellipse.animate.set_stroke(color=ORANGE, width=6))

outline.topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Unveiling Conic Sections
outline.target_audience: High school or undergraduate geometry students

sections.title: Introduction: The Geometry of a Sliced Cone
sections.content: Briefly define a cone and show how slicing it at different angles creates various shapes: circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas. Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres' as the geometric 'Rosetta Stone' that explains why these shapes share the same algebraic properties.
sections.example: Visual: A virtual flashlight beam hitting a wall, changing shape as the angle of the wall tilts relative to the beam.

sections.title: Prerequisite Concept: Tangency and Focus
sections.content: Define the relationship between a sphere and a plane. Key takeaway: Any two tangent lines from a point to a sphere are equal in length. This is the hidden key that bridges the sphere to the conic section.
sections.example: A marble (sphere) touching a glass plate (plane) at exactly one point.

sections.title: The Dandelin Construction
sections.content: Animate the process: Place a sphere inside a cone such that it is tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the slicing plane (at a point F). This point F is the 'focus' of our conic section.
sections.example: An animation of a translucent cone with a glowing sphere inside, showing the point of tangency F appearing on the cut surface.

sections.title: Proving the Ellipse Property
sections.content: Demonstrate that for any point P on the ellipse, the sum of distances to the two foci (PF1 + PF2) is constant. Use the property that segments tangent to the same sphere are equal to prove the distance sum equals the distance between the two circles of tangency.
sections.example: A robotic arm tracing the perimeter of an ellipse, while two lines are drawn from the pen to the two 'hidden' foci, showing their sum remains constant.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-world Application
sections.content: Summarize how this bridge between 3D solids and 2D curves provides a unified vision of geometry. Mention applications in optics (satellite dishes) and orbital mechanics.
sections.example: A satellite dish (parabola) or a comet's orbit around the sun (ellipse), visualized through the lens of the cone-sphere intersection.
